name: BLUUMBIO
long_description:
Our mission

-To ensure current and future generations have access to clean soil, water & air.

-To protect and restore earth's beautiful and diverse ecosystems.

-To undo the harm of industrial activity on the planet and ensure future industrial activities are more sustainable.

Our research

-We develop new bio-based solutions that break down and remove toxic chemicals from the environment.  We also develop bioreactor based solutions which remove toxins from industrial production pipelines, ensuring contaminants are never released into the environment.

-To do this, we've partnered with Nature. Specifically, we have harnessed the power of one of Nature's smallest but most powerful technologies: enzymes. Enzymes are everywhere. They break down the food in your stomach, remove dirt from your clothes, and make our beer. At BluumBio, we look for enzymes found in bacteria, algae, plants and other living organisms that naturally degrade toxic chemicals. We then make these enzymes work better in the lab and come up with develop new applications for these technologies.

launches.title: Vista Space: Structural batteries for high performance spacecraft
launches.tagline: Our batteries let spacecraft have 2x the energy capacity or save 15-30% in volume
launches.body:
### **TL;DR**

**About Us** \
[Vista Space](https://govista.space/) builds Tesla-inspired structural batteries to increase satellites’ energy capacity without increasing their size. The founders worked at SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and NASA. 

**The Ask** \
If you or anyone you know are building spacecraft or any other products that could benefit from structural batteries, we should talk! Please reach out or send referrals our way to [sales@govista.space](mailto:sales@govista.space) or our website at <https://govista.space>. 

—

Hey all, we’re [Vista Space](https://govista.space/), co-founded by [Maxim Kraft](https://linkedin.com/in/maximkraft), [Petar Matejic](https://linkedin.com/in/petar-matejic), and [Chaitanya Kore](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ckore/). Our mission is to power the next generation of space exploration. 

### **Problem**

Power is a fundamental constraint for space mission design, as everything operating in space requires electricity. Today's spacecraft power systems are not capable enough to support both the current and next-generation mission concepts, leading satellite manufacturers to painful trade-offs: **limiting additional hardware** or **increasing system size** to get more power. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79713&key=user_uploads/293472/5a1ec437-b4ee-4544-b3ad-5082e2be92c3)

With reduced capabilities, companies lose their technological advantage. With increased size, manufacturing costs are higher, risk of schedule delays is greater, and go-to-market is slower due to fewer spacecraft launches. **These trade-offs are fundamental limitations** of spacecraft design and space economics. 

While space-rated solar panels are thin, efficient, and can be foldable, **batteries take up significant useful volume** (up to 30% in small spacecraft) **and are vastly less capable** than the latest terrestrial equivalents.  

### **Solution**

Traditional spacecraft walls are purely structural, serving little functional purpose after launch while occupying valuable space. 

Our **Voltaris 1** module replaces these walls, providing **structural support and energy storage simultaneously**. This allows satellite manufacturers to **double their energy capacity** without increasing size or **gain 15-30% more useful volume** at the same power budget. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79713&key=user_uploads/293472/a51852a8-0dfc-46a5-a2bf-049c29a42d7e)

**Key Features:** 

* **Inspired by structural batteries in EVs** like the Tesla Model Y and Cybertruck 
* **Plug and play with any chassis size**, bolting onto the chassis in place of aluminum walls 
* **Compatible with third-party electrical & power system** (EPS) modules inside 
* CubeSat modules **include a solar cell**, and all form factors have the electrical components & thermal protection systems to **work out of the box** 
* **Additional radiation protection** for the contents inside the chassis 
* Launching **to space in February 2025** 
* Targeting **pricing to be middle of the market** for space batteries

 

### **About Us**

Maxim & Petar met at SpaceX, working on Starlink and Starship, respectively, and bonded over discussing opportunities for satellite design improvements. Maxim met Chaitanya at a conference for rising NewSpace leaders and stayed in touch since. 

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79713&key=user_uploads/89898/1b0414fe-b273-4da1-b4fb-2265113278ca)

Maxim: Berkeley alum (Economics & Physics). Former SpaceX, Rocket Lab. Taught a course on space economy and entrepreneurship during undergrad. 

Petar: Former SpaceX, NASA, Firefly, The Boring Company. Co-founded UNLV's student satellite team. 

Chaitanya: Founded Space Force Association Great Lakes chapter. Helped secure a multi-billion-dollar battery gigafactory in Illinois.  

### **The Ask**

* Please share this post with your network, even outside the space industry! 
* If we’re building something you need, please reach out or send referrals to [sales@govista.space](mailto:founders@govista.space) or our website <https://govista.space>.
* Leave an upvote!

 

**Early adopter benefits:** Anyone who places a Pre-order gets personalized technical review sessions and priority delivery of the first production units. 

Thanks all! Let us know what you think.

launches.title: Molagri: Resistance-free pesticides 🪲
launches.tagline: Species-specific biopesticides built from engineered insect viruses, updatable the moment pests develop resistance.
launches.body:
**TLDR:** We build next-generation pesticides from engineered insect virus-like particles. They target a single pest species, stay safe for humans, pollinators, and the environment, and can be reprogrammed over time as pests evolve resistance.

Pesticides underpin modern agriculture and food security, accounting for $80B in annual spend. Without effective pesticides, we can't grow enough food.

<https://youtu.be/6rxXDJeC14Y>

**The Problem 🌱**

Pests are developing resistance faster than new pesticides can be invented to replace the failing ones. At the same time, regulators are banning core active ingredients over environmental and human toxicity. Farmers are losing tools from both ends at once.

**Our Solution 🪲**

We build pesticides out of insect virus-like particles. We start with a virus that only infects insects and is harmless to humans. We strip out its genome so it can't infect or replicate, and we keep the empty protein shell as a delivery vehicle.

We engineer that shell with two parts:

* A **targeting element** that recognizes a single pest species (or a set of species). This is what keeps the product species-specific and invisible to humans, pollinators, and beneficial insects.
* A **payload** that kills the pest.

Both parts are swappable. Changing the targeting element will modify which pest it kills. Changing the payload will result in a new kill mechanism for the same pest, which is how we update the product when resistance appears.

Designing for true pollinator safety is hard, so we did the underlying science ourselves. We solved a cryo-EM structure of a key receptor in honey bees, which lets us deliberately engineer our targeting elements so they do not bind pollinators.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108796&key=user_uploads/2273508/62f4362a-1938-4843-ab26-c9a62c742a84)

**Why Us? 🧑🏽‍🔬**

We are Zaky and Min, viral structural biology PhD candidates and lab mates at the University of Toronto, where we have worked together for the past 6 years studying how viruses interact with their hosts. We have published in Nature Microbiology and Nature Communications, and Min holds the world record for the highest-resolution structure of a coronavirus spike protein.

**Traction 📈**

We have signed our first grower LOI, have more in the pipeline, and produced our first set of viruses for testing. During the batch we also solved a cryo-EM structure of a honey-bee receptor that directly informs our pollinator-safe design.

**Connect with us!**

* **Growers and producers**: if you are fighting resistant pests or losing tools to bans, we would love to talk about your crops and target pests. Reach us at [molagri.com](http://molagri.com) 
* **Everyone else:** intros to ag and crop-science operators, or anyone who has built regulated biological products, are always welcome.

name: Grip
long_description: Grip is a robotics company building intelligent robotic systems for waste and recycling. We are starting with organic waste, where removing contaminants from messy, constantly changing streams remains difficult and highly manual. Our technology combines learning-based manipulation and custom hardware to identify and pick objects, learning from real-world operating data, including every successful and failed grasp, to become more reliable and adaptable over time. This helps waste operators reduce manual sorting, recover more valuable material, lower contamination, and deploy automation flexibly across facilities. Over time, Grip aims to expand beyond organics and build the intelligent manipulation layer for trash in general, making waste processing and the circular economy more efficient and scalable.

launches.title: Grip - Robotics for Waste Management
launches.tagline: Robots that sort any waste and recover recyclables, learning from every grasp.
launches.body:
Hi everyone - Stan and Jonas here, founders of **Grip**. We build intelligent robots that sort _any_ waste, not just the clean, predictable objects existing systems are limited to. We're starting with plastic contamination in organic waste.\
\
<https://youtu.be/qIJ4a49WxpI>

**The problem**

We didn't start with a thesis, we found it on sorting lines, after visiting waste facilities across several countries:

* **Contamination is existential.** Plastic that organic-waste facilities can't remove gets shredded, processed, and spread onto agricultural soil. Operators spend up to 30% of operating costs fighting it and still fall short. Even Germany's 0.1% limit for plastic in finished compost is a tacit admission that full removal isn't possible with today's tools.
* **The labor force is aging and shrinking.** The picking work is unpleasant and turnover is brutal. Operators increasingly aren't choosing between people and robots. They're choosing between robots and nobody.
* **Dangerous items cause fires.** Batteries, propane tanks, and vapes slip through and ignite during handling and shredding: 448 reported fires at US and Canadian waste facilities in 2025, \~$2.5B in damage, and insurers are walking away. At the same time trash sorting is sitting in the top 5 of US deadliest occupations.

**What we built**

The hard part isn't the gripper. It's that waste never looks the way you planned. Objects arrive crushed, folded, tangled, half-buried, and moving. Put today's sorting robots in front of this and they break.

We're building one manipulation system that picks whatever shows up, at the front of the line where the material is most chaotic and existing automation stops. That means chaotic scene understanding, robust grasp planning, and hardware built for real waste streams: our custom three-way gripper is designed to maximize throughput, taking out as much contamination per cycle as possible.

Our rugged hardware matters, but intelligence is the product. Every pick generates data no other system ever encounters: what the robot saw, what it tried, how the material responded, whether it worked.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=111317&key=user_uploads/3678142/bc867fdc-9225-4b85-83f9-f83433465d5b)

**Why now**

Waste policy has moved from vague ambition to enforceable deadlines:

* Separate bio-waste collection is now mandatory across the EU. More material, and more contamination, every year.
* New EU fertiliser rules just cut permitted impurities in compost and digestate, with national limits like Germany's stricter still.
* The US is real: California mandated a 75% cut in landfilled organics, missed it, and enforcement is ramping. At the same time, landfills near major cities are filling up, and that pressure is pushing more and more US municipalities to collect organic waste separately. More material, more contamination, more facilities that need to sort it.

More than 6,500 biowaste plants and thousands of recycling facilities across Europe and North America face this with no robot that can touch it. That's Grip.

**Why us**

We've built autonomous race cars, quadrupeds, drones, and excavators, robots that operate in dirt, weather, and chaos rather than controlled labs. Grip is that experience applied to an industry where physical intelligence removes a real bottleneck.

**Our ask**

We'd love intros to:

* Owners and operators of composting, anaerobic-digestion, and organic-waste facilities
* Owners and operators of MRFs and recycling facilities
* Regulators and experts shaping contamination limits and recycling standards

If someone runs a facility and will show us their hardest sorting problem, we'll get on a plane.

[**griprobotics.ai**](http://griprobotics.ai)
